diseases.name: Anthracnose
diseases.description: A fungal fruit rot of peach that is worst in warm, wet weather near harvest.
diseases.causes: Spores spread by rain splash from infected fruit and nearby hosts; warm, humid weather favours it.
symptoms: Round, sunken, tan to brown spots on the fruit
Rings of orange-pink spore masses in the spots
diseases.effect: Infected fruit is lost, before or after harvest.
diseases.untreated: Mummified fruit carries the fungus to next season.

steps.title: Remove rotting fruit
steps.instruction: Pick off and remove spotted fruit and mummies.
steps.rationale: Each rotting fruit releases masses of spores.

steps.title: Harvest promptly and cool the fruit
steps.instruction: Pick at maturity and keep the fruit cool.
steps.rationale: Rot develops fast in warm fruit.

steps.title: Protective fungicide before harvest
steps.instruction: Spray a registered product on the label's schedule in wet weather.

lifecycle: The fungus survives on mummies and twigs.
Rain splashes spores onto the fruit.
Sunken spots with spore rings form as fruit ripens.
Rotting fruit spreads it to its neighbours.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: peach anthracnose
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Brown Rot
diseases.description: A fungal disease of stone fruit that blights blossoms and rots the fruit.
diseases.causes: Spores from mummified fruit and twig cankers infect blossoms in wet spring weather and ripening fruit near harvest, often through wounds.
symptoms: Soft, light-brown rot spreading fast over the fruit
Tufts of grey-tan spores on the rot
Fruit shrivels into a dry mummy
diseases.effect: Rotted fruit is lost, on the tree and in storage.
diseases.untreated: Mummies and cankers start next year's infections.

steps.title: Remove rotting fruit and mummies
steps.instruction: Pick off rotting fruit and all mummies, also from the ground.
steps.rationale: They are the main spore source.

steps.title: Prune out blighted twigs
steps.instruction: Cut out twigs with cankers well below the damage.

steps.title: Fungicide at bloom and before harvest
steps.instruction: Spray a registered product at the label's timings.
steps.rationale: Blossoms and ripening fruit are the vulnerable stages.

prevention.title: Thin fruit and prune
prevention.detail: Touching fruit passes the rot along.

lifecycle: The fungus overwinters in mummies and cankers.
Spring spores blight the blossoms.
Near harvest, spores infect ripening fruit.
Rotting fruit shrivels into new mummies.
conditions: Wet weather at bloom and harvest.
Mummies left on or under the tree.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: peach brown rot
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Peach Leaf Curl
diseases.description: A fungal disease that thickens, puckers and reddens peach leaves in spring.
diseases.causes: Spores on the bark and buds infect the leaves as the buds open in cool, wet spring weather.
symptoms: Red to purple colour on the puckered areas
Leaves turn powdery grey-white, then drop
diseases.effect: The tree loses its first leaves and must regrow them, which weakens it.
diseases.untreated: Several years of heavy curl weaken the tree and cut the crop.

steps.title: Remove curled leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off and remove curled leaves where practical.
steps.rationale: Reduces spores for next season (the tree regrows leaves).

steps.title: Feed and water the tree
steps.instruction: Water in dry spells and feed lightly to support the new leaves.
steps.rationale: The second flush of leaves is not infected.

steps.title: Spray before bud swell next year
steps.instruction: Apply a registered fungicide at leaf fall or before the buds swell, following the label.
steps.rationale: Spraying after the leaves curl does not help.

prevention.title: Spray at the right time
prevention.detail: Only sprays before bud swell work.

prevention.title: Grow resistant varieties
prevention.detail: Some peaches are much less affected.

lifecycle: Spores overwinter on bark and bud scales.
Cool, wet weather at bud break lets them infect.
Leaves thicken, pucker and turn red.
A grey bloom of new spores forms before the leaves drop.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: peach leaf curl
Content: general plant-pathology knowledge (APS disease compendia, university extension guides, UC IPM); not reviewed by a plant pathologist.

diseases.name: Peach Rust
diseases.description: A rust fungus of peach and other stone fruit leaves.
diseases.causes: Spores blow in or survive in twig cankers; long leaf wetness in warm weather lets them infect.
symptoms: Small, angular yellow spots on the upper leaf
Leaves yellow and drop late in the season
diseases.effect: Early leaf fall weakens the tree for next year.
diseases.untreated: Repeated defoliation reduces vigour and fruit size.

steps.title: Clear fallen leaves
steps.instruction: Rake and remove leaves in autumn.

steps.title: Prune out cankered twigs
steps.instruction: Remove twigs with rust cankers in spring.

steps.title: Fungicide when rust appears early
steps.instruction: Spray a registered product following the label.

lifecycle: Spores survive in twig cankers or blow in.
Wet, warm weather lets them infect leaves.
Yellow spots form, with rust pustules beneath.
New spores spread through the tree.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: peach rust

diseases.name: Peach Scab
diseases.description: A fungal disease that freckles peach fruit with dark spots.
diseases.causes: Spores from twig lesions infect young fruit in warm, wet weather after petal fall; spots appear weeks later.
symptoms: Small olive-green to black spots on the fruit, near the stem end
Fruit skin cracks over the blotches
diseases.effect: Fruit is blemished and may crack and rot.
diseases.untreated: Twig lesions carry the fungus to next year.

steps.title: Prune out infected twigs
steps.instruction: Remove twigs with scab lesions in winter.

steps.title: Fungicide from petal fall
steps.instruction: Spray a registered product on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Young fruit is infected in the first weeks.

lifecycle: The fungus overwinters in twig lesions.
Spring rain spreads spores to young fruit.
Spots appear about 6 weeks later.
Spots join and the skin cracks.
conditions: Warm, wet weather after petal fall.
Twig lesions left in the tree.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: peach scab
